title: Other websites could submit contact enquiries through visitors' browsers
description: POST /api/contact read the body as text and parsed JSON without checking Content-Type or the request origin. A text/plain POST is a CORS simple request, so any site could make its visitors' browsers send enquiries, each from a different IP, which also sidesteps the per-IP limit.
root_cause: No same-origin gate (Content-Type or Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin) before processing the body.
intended_behavior: Only the site's own contact form should be able to submit an enquiry from a browser.

trace.description: request.text() then JSON.parse regardless of type.
Email sent for the cross-site request.

evidence.description: Body read with no Content-Type check at 26427a8.
Mocked Resend received the payload for a text/plain cross-site request.

conditions.description: A visitor opens an attacker page while RESEND_API_KEY is configured.

instructions: Start next start locally with a dummy key and the mock-resend.mjs fetch mock.
Send the POST with content-type text/plain and sec-fetch-site cross-site (see repro-contact.sh).
Observe 200 and a mocked email at baseline; 415/403 after the fix.
execution.observed_result: Baseline: {"ok":true} and an email payload built. Fixed: 415 unsupported_media_type and 403 forbidden.

remediation.strategy: Reject Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site and require application/json (forces a CORS preflight that the route never approves). Commit ca03825.

likelihood.reason: Needs only a page the visitor opens.

impact.reason: Spam to one inbox and Resend quota use; no data exposure.

confidence.reason: Reproduced locally against the baseline build.

title: Submitting the contact form before JavaScript loads put personal details in the URL
description: The contact form is prerendered and had no method attribute. A submit before hydration (slow network, JS blocked) made the browser GET /contact?name=...&email=...&company=...&message=..., exposing the visitor's details in browser history, Vercel request logs and the Referer of later requests. Found by the independent verifier.
root_cause: Form element without method relies on JavaScript preventDefault.
intended_behavior: Personal details are only ever sent in a request body.

evidence.description: <form noValidate onSubmit={onSubmit}> at 26427a8; inputs carry name attributes.

conditions.description: Visitor submits before hydration or with JavaScript disabled.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anyone who can read URLs later (shared device history, log readers).
instructions: Run nojs-submit.cjs (Playwright, javaScriptEnabled false) against a local build.
execution.observed_result: Fixed build: POST to /contact, URL stays /contact. Baseline default method is GET per HTML spec, putting fields in the query string.

remediation.strategy: Add method="post" to the form. Commit bcac652.

likelihood.reason: Needs a submit inside the pre-hydration window.

impact.reason: Exposes one visitor's own contact details to logs/history.

confidence.reason: HTML default method and local no-JS check.

title: Rate limit is per server instance, so total email volume depends on Vercel settings
description: The 5-per-10-minutes limit lives in an in-memory Map, so each Vercel instance and each cold start has its own counter. A determined sender can exceed it across instances and flood ask@daveroai.com or use up Resend quota.
claimed_root_cause: Per-process limiter with no shared store or platform rule.

trace.description: const hits = new Map() per instance.

blockers: Instance count and any Vercel Firewall/WAF rate-limit or BotID rules are deployment settings not in the repository.

validation_plan.local: Not reproducible meaningfully on one local process.
validation_plan.deployment: Add a Vercel Firewall rate-limit rule on POST /api/contact (e.g. 5 per 10 minutes per IP, action deny) and optionally BotID; then the in-app limiter is a second layer.

title: Email check accepted address lists used as reply_to
description: The email regex allowed commas and angle brackets, e.g. 'a,victim@evil.example', which was sent as reply_to.
reason: The sender already chooses reply_to freely, so a list crosses no new boundary: staff would see the addresses before replying. Tightened anyway in commit 9c909d3 as input hygiene.

title: CR/LF in name or company reached the email subject sent to Resend
description: validateField only trimmed and length-checked name and company, so CR/LF and other control characters were placed in the subject passed to Resend. Whether Resend turns them into extra headers (for example Bcc) is outside the repository.
claimed_root_cause: No control-character rejection on single-line fields used in the subject.

trace.description: Subject built from data.name and data.company.

evidence.description: Only trim and length checks at 26427a8.
Mocked Resend received subject 'Website enquiry from Eve\r\nBcc: x@evil.example, Acme'.

blockers: How Resend's API encodes CR/LF in the subject field is not visible in source and must not be tested by sending real email.

validation_plan.local: Fixed in source anyway (commit 9c909d3): control characters now return 400 before any email is built.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner can confirm with Resend documentation or support that the subject is header-encoded; no action needed after the fix.

title: Contact API buffered the whole request body before enforcing the 10 KB cap
description: With no Content-Length (chunked upload) the route called request.text(), holding the full body in memory before the byteLength check.
root_cause: Size check after a full read.
intended_behavior: Reading stops as soon as 10 KB is exceeded.

evidence.description: request.text() before the byteLength check at line 31.

conditions.description: Upper bound is the platform request body limit, so impact is memory per request, not unbounded.

payloads: 2 MB body sent with Transfer-Encoding: chunked
instructions: Pipe 2 MB to POST /api/contact with chunked encoding (repro-contact.sh step 4).
execution.observed_result: Baseline returned 413 only after reading the full body; fixed build cancels the stream at 10 KB.

remediation.strategy: Stream the body with a capped reader and cancel past 10 KB. Commit ca03825.

impact.reason: Extra memory per request up to the platform body limit.

title: Rate limit keyed on a spoofable X-Forwarded-For
description: The limiter keys on the first X-Forwarded-For entry, which a client could forge if passed through.
claimed_root_cause: Trusting a client header for identity.
reason: Vercel overwrites x-forwarded-for and does not forward client-supplied values (vercel.com/docs/headers/request-headers), so the value is the real client IP in the intended deployment.

title: Dependency advisories (minimatch GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, deepmerge GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4)
description: npm audit reported 13 issues (11 moderate, 2 low) through eslint/typescript-eslint and the shadcn CLI (ts-morph, @shadcn/registry), and shadcn sat in runtime dependencies.
claimed_root_cause: Vulnerable transitive packages; CLI listed as a runtime dependency.

evidence.description: shadcn in dependencies; site code imports only shadcn/tailwind.css at build time.

reason: None of these packages is imported by shipped server or client code; they run only in lint or the shadcn CLI on developer input. Hygiene fixed anyway (commit 94769ae): shadcn moved to devDependencies, minimatch overridden to 11.0.5; npm audit now 3 low (deepmerge, no patched release exists), npm audit --omit=dev 0.

title: No browser security headers; any site could frame the pages
description: next.config.ts set no headers. Responses had no CSP, X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy, and advertised X-Powered-By: Next.js.
root_cause: No headers() config and poweredByHeader left on.
intended_behavior: Pages refuse framing and send a restrictive baseline policy.

evidence.description: curl -I / at baseline showed only X-Powered-By among security headers.

conditions.description: Clickjacking needs a visitor on an attacker page that frames the site.

execution.attacker_perspective: Third-party website embedding the site in an iframe.
instructions: curl -sI the home page and look for frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options.
execution.observed_result: Baseline: none present. Fixed: CSP (frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options DENY, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP; X-Powered-By removed.

remediation.strategy: Add headers() in next.config.ts with a no-nonce CSP (nonces would disable static prerendering/PPR) and poweredByHeader:false. Commit d38a31e.

likelihood.reason: Needs a lure page and a click.

impact.reason: The only state-changing action is sending an enquiry.

confidence.reason: Observed on the local production build.
